title: Memcached and how it compares with Redis

videos.script: Redis does many things. Memcached does one. It keeps bytes under a key, in memory, for as long as it has room. {{one}} No types. No disk. No replication. When it restarts, it is empty, and that is the design. {{empty}} What it does have is threads. Every core of the server answers requests at once. {{threads}} In this lesson you speak its protocol by hand, one line of text at a time. You watch it forget the oldest values when memory fills. {{forget}} Then you spread one cache over two servers, and count how many keys move when a third one joins. {{many}} And at the end you choose between Memcached and Redis, for reasons rather than habit. {{choose}}
